header.running_head: The Marriages of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: "What have you seen, O Aa'isha?" "I have seen only a Jewess!" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied. "Do not say that," Rasulullaah ﷺ warned, "She has accepted Islaam and is an excellent Muslim." [^1]

Hadhrat Sa'eed bin Musayyib narrates that when Hadhrat Safiyya bint Huyay (RA) arrived (in Madinah), she was wearing gold earrings in the shape of palm leaves. She however gave these as a gift to (Rasulullaah ﷺ's daughter) Hadhrat Faatima (RA) and some other ladies who were with her. [^2]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Marriage to Hadhrat Juwayriyya Bint Haarith Khuzaa'ee (RA)

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates that when the captives of the Banu Mustaliq tribe were distributed (amongst the Muslim army), Hadhrat Juwayriyyah bint Haarith (RA) happened to fall in the lot of Hadhrat Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas (RA) or one of his nephews. (Rather than being a conventional slave) Hadhrat Juwayriyyah (RA) entered into a contract of Kitaabah [^3] with him. She was an extremely pleasant and beautiful woman who attracted anyone who saw her. Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "She one day came to Rasulullaah ﷺ to seek assistance with paying off her Kitaabah. By Allaah! I disliked her as soon as I saw her standing at the door of my room because I knew that Rasulullaah ﷺ would also see in her what I saw. When she entered the room, she said, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I am Juwayriyyah the daughter of Haarith bin Abu Diraar the leader of his tribe. As you well know, a calamity has befallen me (when I was captured and taken as a slave). I fell to the lot of Thaabit bin Qais bin Shammaas and entered into a contract of Kitaabah with him. I have now come to seek your assistance to pay of the Kitaabah.'"

"Do you not want something better?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "What is that, O Rasulullaah ﷺ?" she wanted to know. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "That I should pay off your Kitaabah and then marry you." "Certainly, O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" she replied, "I am most willing."

When the news reached the Sahabah (RA) that Rasulullaah ﷺ had married Hadhrat Juwayriyyah (RA), they said, "They (the tribe of Hadhrat Juwayriyyah (RA)) are now the in-laws of Rasulullaah ﷺ so free those of them whom you own (as your slaves)." Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "It was therefore as a result of Rasulullaah ﷺ's marriage to Juwayriyyah (RA) that a hundred families of the Banu Mustaliq tribe were set free. I do not know of any woman who was a greater blessing for her tribe than Juwayriyyah (RA)." [^4]
Hadhrat Urwa (RA) reports that Hadhrat Juwayriyyah bint Haarith (RA) said, "Three days before the arrival of Rasulullaah ﷺ I dreamt that the moon came
A contract between slave and master by which the slave has to gradually pay the master a certain sum of money to secure freedom.

Ibn Is'haaq, as quoted in Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.5 Pg.159). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.8 Pg.116) has reported a similar narration in which he names Safwaan bin Maalik as the former husband of Hadhrat Juwayriyyah (RA). Haakim (Vol.4 Pg.26) has also reported the narration.
